translation_notes: target.remove((None, None, None)) -- the 'empty this graph' idiom -- becomes -{ ?s ?p ?o }(target): shorter, and it says which three positions are free instead of leaving the reader to count Nones. The call suffix was preferred to a '@graph target' declaration because this is the function's only island while 'target' is still named by .add() and .bind() below: a declaration would have added a line without removing one.

NOT TRANSLATED, and it is a finding: 'for triple in incoming: target.add(triple)' stays rdflib. The triple is an opaque 3-tuple that arrives as a value; +{ } takes a written pattern, and the only way to force it would be +{ {triple[0]} {triple[1]} {triple[2]} }(target), which is longer and less clear than the .add() it replaces. Copying already-built triples has no island -- the migration guide covers the whole-graph case ('g += other' unchanged) but not its per-triple form.

the mechanical draft had added '@prefix rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#> .' because RDF appears in the region's context import line; the region body never uses rdf:, so the declaration was dropped and the import line kept verbatim. A prefix declared for an unused import is noise the surface metrics would have counted.

restored binding (AGENT_BATCH): the extracted context carried '_logger = logging.getLogger("acquirium.graph_store")' but not 'import logging'; the line is added to original.py, identically on both sides, or neither module runs.

driver: 'self' is a stand-in carrying the query Dataset the region binds prefixes on, and it compares by those prefixes -- graph isomorphism cannot see a namespace binding, so without this the second half of the region would be unobserved. Three calls: replace=True on a non-empty target, replace=False (merge), replace=True with an empty incoming (the target must end up empty). Negative control run: turning the island into 'pass' makes the driver report 'graphs not isomorphic (5 vs 7)' and '(0 vs 2)'.

repair.driver: cinq appels où la cible est, comme dans le dépôt (graph_store.py:669, 897, 965), un graphe nommé d'un Dataset default_union=False tenant aussi un graphe par défaut et un autre graphe source avec des voisins à deux termes communs et un triplet identique ; store en mémoire enregistreur des `remove` (motif et contexte) ; égalité sur tous les graphes du Dataset, le journal du store, les liaisons du Dataset source (où tombe `target.bind`) et du Dataset de requête ; description à nœuds anonymes imbriqués dans la cible ; replace faux, entrant vide, cible inexistante, conflit de préfixe et d'espace (`exo:`/`ex:`) pour `override=False` ; journal `acquirium.graph_store` capturé et comparé.
mutants_killed: receveur élargi au store entier (Dataset default_union=True) (survivait)
vidage triplet par triplet au lieu d'un seul `remove((None, None, None))` (survivait ; même effet RDF, tué par le journal du store)
`override=True` sur `target.bind` et sur la liaison du Dataset de requête (survivaient)
îlot -> `pass` ; `-{ ?s a ?o }` ; garde forcée à True / à False ; receveur = graphe par défaut du store

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the per-triple copy loop becomes `target += incoming` (Graph.__iadd__, one addN with the target as context: same triples in the target, and the store's remove log is unchanged); the two wrapped calls of the bind loop are put on one line each. The try/except around the two binds and the debug log are kept as they were.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `@graph target` + `-{ ?s ?p ?o }` for the clear (119 tokens against 122 with the call suffix `-{ ?s ?p ?o }(target)`; no @prefix is in scope, so @graph binds nothing on the target). `target += incoming` stays: no island copies a graph.
No exception to the symmetry rule.
